title: Cold spray manufacturing of oxide-dispersion strengthened (ODS) steels using gas-atomized and ball-milled 14YWT powders

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Chemical_Composition: Bal. Fe, 14 wt% Cr, 3 wt% W, 0.4 wt% Ti, 0.2 wt% Y, 0.25 wt% O
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: spherical, with equiaxed grains and very small Fe-Y intermetallic compound particles within grains

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: grinding and polishing them to a final polishing step with 0.02 μm colloidal silica suspension (pH 10.5) Microhardness in ASTM E384 accordance. Al substrates removed by dissolving in 20% NaOH solution.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: high population of ultrafine grains in the size range of ∼ 200 nm formed at the particle boundaries due to dynamic recrystallization whereas partially deformed grains were observed in the central regions of the particles. recrystallization occurred and presence of elongated grains with random orientation, discontinuous Ti-Y-N rich layers

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Chemical_Composition: Bal. Fe, 14 wt% Cr, 3 wt %W, 0.4 wt% Ti, 0.2 wt% Y, 0.25 wt% O
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: spherical, with equiaxed grains and very small Fe-Y intermetallic compound particles within grains

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: heat treated at 900°C for one hour in a vacuum (10^-3 Pa)
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: grinding and polishing them to a final polishing step with 0.02 μm colloidal silica suspension (pH 10.5) Microhardness in ASTM E384 accordance. Al substrates removed by dissolving in 20% NaOH solution.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: recrystallization occurred and presence of elongated grains with random orientation, discontinuous Ti-Y-N rich layers. interparticle interfaces were not observed and equiaxed grains formed. Both fine-pores and submicron sized precipitates were identified along the grain boundaries. The unbonded interparticle interfaces appeared to coalesce and form fine pores.

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Chemical_Composition: Bal. Fe, 14 wt% Cr, 3 wt% W, 0.4 wt% Ti, 0.2 wt% Y, 0.125 wt% O
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: very fine grain structure (80 ± 10 nm), elongated grains
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Production_Method: gas-atomized powder ball milled with FeO
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Heat_Treatment_Description: Cryogenic milling in a liquid nitrogen bath (-196°C for 6h) followed by annealing at 1000°C for 30 min in a hydrogen and argon environment.

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: grinding and polishing them to a final polishing step with 0.02 μm colloidal silica suspension (pH 10.5) Microhardness in ASTM E384 accordance. Al substrates removed by dissolving in 20% NaOH solution.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: very fine grain structures. severe plastic deformation resulting in refined grain size and dislocation forest in the grains. nanoprecipitate particles were observed (~8 nm), as well as second pase particles of Cr, Y-Ti or Ti oxides.

Experiments.Notes: BM-CM-HT-1000. the paper used Al 6061 and 316L as substrates, but the results did not differentiate the two. I put down Al 6061 since it was noted it dissolves in NaOH and they obtained samples that way. Other temperatures were used to anneal powders but not used to make any coating samples.

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Chemical_Composition: Bal. Fe, 14 wt% Cr, 3 wt% W, 0.4 wt% Ti, 0.2 wt% Y, 0.125 wt% O
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: irregular and angular, slight agglomeration, very fine grain structure with high density of dislocation entanglement, fairly equiaxed with a size of 1.6 ± 0.3 μm
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Production_Method: gas-atomized powder ball milled with FeO
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Heat_Treatment_Description: Cryogenic milling in a liquid nitrogen bath (-196°C for 6h) followed by annealing at 1100°C for 30 min in a hydrogen and argon environment.

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: grinding and polishing them to a final polishing step with 0.02 μm colloidal silica suspension (pH 10.5) Microhardness in ASTM E384 accordance. Al substrates removed by dissolving in 20% NaOH solution.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: bimodal distribution of grain size, consisting of fine grains with a size of ∼ 150 nm and coarser grains with a size ∼ 370 nm. The relatively large grains surrounded by the fine grains showed high density of dislocations. severe plastic deformation resulting in refined grain size and dislocation forest in the grains. nanoprecipitate particles were observed (~19 nm), as well as second pase particles of Cr, Y-Ti or Ti oxides.

Experiments.Notes: BM-CM-HT-1100. the paper used Al 6061 and 316L as substrates, but the results did not differentiate the two. I put down Al 6061 since it was noted it dissolves in NaOH and they obtained samples that way. The text states the powders were heat treated for an hours while some figures say it was 30 minutes.
